headline: Man City found guilty; Arsenal, Liverpool have injury scares
paragraphs: Manchester City were found guilty by an independent Premier League commission of all charges relating to financial rule breaches between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons. The Guardian and BBC Sport report the commission found City used "sham" contracts to inflate revenue by around 900m pounds; City say they will appeal before Friday's deadline, per the Guardian. CEO Ferran Soriano declined to answer questions from BBC Sport and Sky Sports at a Copenhagen conference, though Sky Sports reports he later sent an internal message to staff and players.

Two of the six clubs had injury scares over the international break. Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard missed Norway training after what Sky Sports called an "ugly" tackle from Silva; FourFourTwo separately reports Arsenal are in "continuous contact" with the Norway camp over his ankle. Liverpool's Cody Gakpo withdrew from the Netherlands squad with an ankle injury picked up in what FourFourTwo calls an "industrial tackle" on international duty, also reported by Sky Sports. Neither outlet gives a timeline for return.

Transfer gossip touched four of the six tracked clubs but stayed at rumour level. BBC's gossip column links Arsenal and Manchester United with Porto's Alberto Costa and says Liverpool retain interest in Real Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni; it credits "BBC Sport" as a second source, but that is the same newsroom, not independent confirmation. The same column has Real Madrid's Trent Alexander-Arnold staying put, while Sky's newspaper round-up says Madrid's Raul Asencio rejected summer interest from Chelsea and Liverpool. Bayern have twice been linked with Barcelona's Dani Olmo, also single-sourced.
